title: KV cooperative bucket sharding for topology-aware multi-GPU pipeline
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem statement: For mixed tensor/pipeline parallel topologies, KV cache memory is fragmented across GPUs resulting in uneven headroom, unnecessary spills, and p99 latency spikes when hot prefixes are routed to overloaded shards. This ticket proposes a cooperative bucket sharding approach: group KV entries into lightweight buckets that can be remapped, replicated, or migrated across GPUs at runtime based on topology-aware heuristics and pipeline stage ownership. The solution must preserve deterministic KV lookup semantics for inference, minimize cross-GPU memcpy, and avoid stalls during continuous batching.
proposed_solution:
1) Bucketization: bucket keys by prefix fingerprint into fixed-capacity buckets (configurable bucket-size). Buckets are the unit of placement (not individual KV entries).
2) Cooperative remapping controller: a lightweight per-node coordinator maintains a compact placement table mapping bucket -> home shard (GPU). The controller uses GPU topology (NVLink/PCIe), current memory headroom, and pipeline stage locality to prefer local placement.
3) Hot-bucket replication: for buckets with high access skew we spawn a read-only replica on adjacent GPUs (prefer NVLink neighbors) using a lease to guarantee eventual consistency for appending kv entries during generation.
4) Lazy migration: when headroom imbalance exceeds threshold, migrator performs zero-copy pointer handover where possible or batched memcpy with backpressure to the batching pipeline to avoid stalls.
5) Prefetch hints & pipeline hooks: the scheduler annotates upcoming requests with bucket access patterns (from prefix cache predictions) enabling overlap of prefetch and compute across pipeline stages.
6) Eviction/compaction: per-bucket compaction to reclaim space and prioritize cold-key evictions globally using a coordinated LRU epoch counter propagated in-batch.
tradeoffs:
- Bucketing trades finer-grained hot-key handling for simpler placement and lower metadata overhead.
- Replication reduces remote fetches but increases memory usage; replication policy must be conservative and adaptive.
- Lease semantics simplify consistency but add transient write path complexity; chosen lease window must balance staleness against write throughput.
- Coordinated remapping introduces control-plane messages; design uses compact diffs and piggybacks on existing routing updates to minimize overhead.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for bucket hashing, placement table consistency, and lease semantics.
2) Microbenchmarks across a range of topologies (2-GPU NVLink, 4-GPU ring, heterogeneous memory sizes) measuring p50/p90/p99 token latency, kv hit rate, and memory headroom variance.
3) End-to-end sim with synthetic skewed prefix workloads (Zipf with varying alpha) and real prompts from our prompt corpus.
4) Fault injection: simulate GPU preemption and network congestion to validate lazy migration and replica fallback.
5) A/B with baseline (current slab-based allocator) on dedicated cluster; track cost per token and percent of requests requiring cross-GPU memcpy.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 1: Feature gated compile-time with runtime flag off. Deploy on canary pool with synthetic workload. Monitor stability for 72h.
- Stage 2: Enable read-only replication only; evaluate memory delta and hit-rate improvements.
- Stage 3: Enable full lazy migration and lease writes for selected models with low write contention (short prompt generation).
- Stage 4: Gradual traffic ramp, expose metrics to console (bucket_migrations, bucket_replicas, kv_remote_fetch_rate), and run performance regression suite before full rollout.
acceptance_criteria: p99 token latency no worse than baseline for balanced workloads
>=20% reduction in cross-GPU memcpy for Zipf-alpha>=1.2 workloads
memory headroom variance across GPUs reduced by >=30% for heterogeneous clusters
no production API compatibility changes (same KV lookup semantics)
Automated canary checks and dashboards added to Console
